test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 05
subject: general
question: A car travels (1)/(3) of the distance on a straight road at a speed of 10 km/h, the next (1)/(3) at a speed of 20 km/h and the last (1)/(3) at a speed of 60 km/h. Find the average speed of the car.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal distance segments, assume the distance of each segment is the **LCM** of given speeds.

LCM of 10, 20, and 60 = 60 km. Let each 1/3 distance be 60 km.

Total Distance = 3 × 60 = 180 km.

Total Time = (60 ÷ 10) + (60 ÷ 20) + (60 ÷ 60) = 6 + 3 + 1 = 10 hours.

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 180 ÷ 10 = 18 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speeds v₁ = 10 km/h, v₂ = 20 km/h, v₃ = 60 km/h for three equal parts of the distance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c2d1cef1999e13f97f99f6317b641b8fe779c0326cc7ced44769a09bff91e15.png] 

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let the total distance be D km.

⇒ Time for first 1/3 distance (t₁) = (D/3) ÷ 10 = D/30 hours.

⇒ Time for second 1/3 distance (t₂) = (D/3) ÷ 20 = D/60 hours.

⇒ Time for last 1/3 distance (t₃) = (D/3) ÷ 60 = D/180 hours.

⇒ Total Time = D/30 + D/60 + D/180

⇒ Total Time = (6D + 3D + D) ÷ 180 = 10D ÷ 180 = D/18 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = D ÷ (D/18) = 18 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, the average speed is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (s₁ − s₂). In opposite directions, it is the sum (s₁ + s₂).</p
